architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed heavy shadow effects and replaced with subtle inset borders for chat containers to create a cleaner, more modern interface
architecture_decisions.rationale: The previous shadow-2xl with neutral-900/15 created a heavy visual weight that distracted from the chat content. Using inset borders with rgba(0,0,0,0.08) provides a subtle separation without visual noise, aligning with modern design systems that favor minimalism and content-first approaches.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Wrapped ChatInterface component in a dedicated div with explicit background and overflow handling to isolate chat area from container styling
architecture_decisions.rationale: Previously, the ChatInterface inherited container styles directly, which caused styling conflicts and made it difficult to maintain consistent backgrounds. By adding a wrapper div with explicit bg-white and h-full, we ensure the chat area has a clean white background regardless of parent container changes, improving component encapsulation.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Simplified file state management by removing the allowedEntries intermediate variable and adding existence checks before updating file status
architecture_decisions.rationale: The previous implementation used an intermediate allowedEntries array to track which files were actually added after the MAX_FILES limit, but this created complexity and potential race conditions. The new approach directly updates state with slice(0, MAX_FILES) and adds a defensive check (prev.some(f => f.id === entry.id)) before updating file status, ensuring we only update files that still exist in the current state.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the intermediate tracking but improving it
Using React refs to track allowed files

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added defensive programming to prevent updating state for files that may have been removed due to MAX_FILES limit
architecture_decisions.rationale: When users drop multiple files exceeding MAX_FILES, some files get sliced out. The previous code could attempt to update status for files that no longer exist in state. The new check ensures we only update files that are still present, preventing unnecessary state updates and potential errors.
alternatives_considered: Using abort controllers for cancelled uploads

tickets.title: Chat UI Consistency Refinement
tickets.description: Update chat bubble and embedded chat components to use cleaner visual styling with subtle borders instead of heavy shadows, and properly isolate chat interface background

tickets.title: File Upload State Management Improvement
tickets.description: Fix file upload state handling to properly manage multiple file drops, enforce MAX_FILES limit, and prevent state updates for removed files

implementation_summary:
The changes implement a more robust file upload system for support tickets while refining the chat UI for better consistency. The file upload improvements focus on state management - instead of using an intermediate allowedEntries array to track which files were added after applying the MAX_FILES limit, the implementation now directly updates the state with slice(0, MAX_FILES) and adds a defensive check before updating individual file statuses. This prevents race conditions where upload callbacks might try to update files that have been removed due to the limit.

For UI consistency, both chat bubble and embedded chat components were updated to use subtler visual styling. The heavy shadow-2xl was replaced with a subtle inset border using rgba(0,0,0,0.08), creating a cleaner, more modern look that aligns with contemporary design systems. Additionally, the ChatInterface component was wrapped in a dedicated div with explicit background and sizing properties to ensure proper isolation from container styles, preventing visual conflicts and maintaining a consistent white background for the chat area.

The changes follow React best practices by keeping state updates atomic and adding defensive checks, while the UI refinements demonstrate attention to design consistency across different chat implementations. The approach maintains backward compatibility while improving both functionality and aesthetics.
